horizons_years_meta.rationale: Current Thesis / Primary Optimization / Persistence horizons.

initial_growth.rationale: Q2 Premium revenue grew 15% YoY with Premium subscribers +9% and ARPU +7%. Mode 14% recognizes both subscriber and pricing origins while avoiding mechanical addition of the two growth rates; tails capture pricing elasticity, mix/FX and engagement uncertainty.

long_run_growth_y8.rationale: Scaled subscription growth mean-reverts toward mature high-single digits with upside from penetration, bundles and pricing.

growth_half_life_years_meta.rationale: Subscriber and pricing growth normalize over several annual pricing/product cycles.

latent_loading_meta.rationale: Premium growth has meaningful shared consumer/platform exposure but substantial company-specific pricing and engagement risk.

initial_growth.rationale: Q2 Ad-Supported revenue grew only 1% while Ad-Supported MAUs grew 14%. D1 therefore receives a wide monetization tail: downside allows continuing direct-channel weakness; upside allows biddable/automated monetization to catch up with audience growth.

long_run_growth_y8.rationale: Long-run advertising growth can range from structural under-monetization to successful scaled automated advertising.

growth_half_life_years_meta.rationale: Advertising cycles and monetization fixes mean-revert faster than subscription scale.

latent_loading_meta.rationale: Advertising is more exposed to common digital-ad and macro demand cycles than Premium.

terminal_margin_Y5.rationale: Current FCF is positive, but content royalties remain the dominant cost base. The range spans renewed content/product-cost pressure through continued gross-margin and operating leverage; center is not price-implied.

terminal_margin_Y8.rationale: Long-run platform scale can modestly improve cash conversion, but royalty/content economics cap software-like margins.

half_life_years_meta.rationale: Cash margins are already mature-positive and should converge over a few reporting cycles.

shock_sigma_meta.rationale: Quarterly content-cost, advertising mix, working-capital and product-spend uncertainty; separate from Joint Layer.

shock_persistence_meta.rationale: Content and monetization shocks persist across adjacent quarters but mean-revert.

lower_bound_meta.rationale: Severe but still positive mature-state cash-margin floor; discrete business-model break belongs to failure/recalibration logic.

upper_bound_meta.rationale: Caps extrapolation well below gross margin after content, operating costs and taxes.

multiple.rationale: Near-term premium possible if monetization and cash margins hold; wide lower tail reflects consumer/content and rate risk.
Mature global subscription/media platform multiple with net cash and recurring revenue, constrained by content royalties and ad cyclicality.
Further duration compression as audience/subscriber growth matures.

Revenue-bridge reference multiple under parity-gated valuation, not an emergency-only fallback. Mode 4.3x / Y5 FCF multiple 24x implies ~17.9% parity margin, intentionally close to the 18% Y5 margin center.

factor_correlations_meta.rationale: Engagement/monetization, cash margin and valuation co-move, but content economics and ad cycles retain independent components.

default_loading_meta.rationale: Scaled platform has meaningful common demand/market exposure with material company-specific consumer, pricing and content risk.

annualized_sigma_meta.rationale: High-duration consumer internet equity path noise, used only for drawdown/path diagnostics and not terminal calibration.

valuation_mean_reversion_half_life_years.rationale: Liquid platform-equity valuation dislocations can mean-revert over several quarters.

implied_revenue_cagr_5y_meta.formula: Local deterministic preflight of Reverse Valuation v1.2.0-style equity-FCF equation from SPOT_calibration_v1.0.yaml; host run_ref remains authoritative.

discount_rate_meta.rationale: Inherited from SPOT RV base calibration.

perturbations_meta.formula: v1.1.2 local robustness: sigma_eq=(Q84-Q16)/2; growth=base-revenue-weighted RMS segment initial_growth sigma_eq; margin=Y5 terminal margin sigma_eq; multiple=Y5 log-space sigma_eq; perturbation=0.25*sigma with accepted ceilings.

persistence_meta.rationale: Consumer engagement, pricing execution, ad monetization and content economics persist across adjacent quarters.

meta.rationale: Digital-ad demand directly changes Ad-Supported monetization; effect is deliberately concentrated on the ad segment.
D1 central case assumes ad demand does not deteriorate materially while automated channels scale.
Adverse direction is weaker digital-ad demand.

Adverse direction is tighter/less supportive capital markets.

Adverse direction is higher rates.
Higher AI/cloud service economics are a small infrastructure/personalization cost pressure; explicitly not a Spotify revenue driver.
Adverse direction is higher AI/cloud pricing because SPOT exposure is cost-side.

scenario_persistence_override.innovation_formula: eta_d,t = standardize(sum(lambda_d,r * u_r,t) + w_d * epsilon_d,t), with u_r,t root innovations after the current phase root-correlation state and epsilon_d,t the same driver idiosyncratic innovation used by BASE
scenario_persistence_override.initialization: when override begins, y_d,t-1 equals the last emitted standardized driver shock; do not initialize to zero
scenario_persistence_override.ramp_rule: numeric-to-numeric rho is linearly interpolated by phase weight; null is bypass and is not interpreted as rho=0
scenario_persistence_override.validation_rule: on a constant-rho plateau after warm-up, Var(y) must remain approximately 1 and empirical lag-1 correlation must approximate rho; insufficient plateau length is diagnostic, not failure

driver_generation.explicit_idiosyncratic_rule: These taxonomy drivers intentionally have no root mapping in v1.1. They retain independent standardized driver innovations; scenario mean/volatility overrides may still apply if a scenario explicitly names them. No root covariance is implied until a future normative reissue adds a mapping.
